Reasoning surface

Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries

Erdős #257

How to read this document

This is a reasoning surface, not an exhaustive corpus export or a literature survey. It exposes the principal premises, method boundaries, and open interfaces; the machine-readable corpus remains the current inventory when later theorem waves outrun the exposition. Three conventions carry the paper’s claim boundary.

Every statement is tagged. [Lean] means a proof term was checked by the pinned Lean kernel. [Cert] means an exact finite computation, with no floating-point decision anywhere in it. [Math] means proved in ordinary mathematics in the sources but not formalised. [Cited] means established in the published literature. [Open] means not proved. These are never blurred, and a statement carrying one band is never described in language belonging to another.

Every parameter-indexed statement is tagged scale:fixed (proved at specific listed values), scale:bounded (proved below an explicit bound), scale:cofinal (proved for arbitrarily large parameters), or scale:uniform (proved for all parameters). The corpus contains theorems at all four scales; the unresolved endpoints require particular infinite-orbit or cofinal hypotheses that are not proved. Sorting by scale keeps that boundary visible.

Every statement records the representation it is expressed in. An obstruction is a fact about a coordinate, not about the object, and a wall measured in one representation may simply not exist in another; the atlas section gives the transport maps, so any obstruction recorded here can be re-measured elsewhere.

The catalogue uses for an unproved hypothesis that would supply a missing step, for a proved implication that uses such a hypothesis, for an exact identity or reduction, and for the precise place where the missing hypothesis enters. These are local navigation terms, not additional mathematical objects or evidence classes.

Erdős Problem 257 is open. No section of this document claims otherwise, and a reduction of the problem to another statement is recorded as a reduction, never as progress toward a solution.

The problem, and what is actually known

The object and the two exact statements

For an integer n≥2n \ge 2 set xn:=1/(2n−1)x_n := 1/(2^n-1), and for A⊆{2,3,4,…}A \subseteq \{2,3,4,\dots\} write xA:=∑n∈Axnx_A := \sum_{n \in A} x_n; the sum always converges, since xn=O(2−n)x_n = O(2^{-n}). Erdős’s Problem #257 asks a single universally quantified question about this family.

Definition 1 (Universal #257, written (U)). Is xA=∑n∈A1/(2n−1)x_A = \sum_{n \in A} 1/(2^n-1) irrational for infinite A⊆ℕA \subseteq \mathbb{N}? OPEN. [Open]

Definition 2 (The half-value question, written (H)). Let the be 𝒜:={y∈ℝ:∃A⊆ℕ,0∉A,y=∑n∈Axn}\mathcal{A} := \{\, y \in \mathbb{R} : \exists A \subseteq \mathbb{N},\ 0 \notin A,\ y = \sum_{n \in A} x_n \,\} (). Is 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A}? OPEN. [Open]

The two are joined by one elementary and completely one-sided implication. Every 2n−12^n-1 is odd, so every subset sum of {xn}\{x_n\} has odd reduced denominator and cannot equal 1/21/2 (). Hence a witness to 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A} is necessarily an infinite AA with xA=1/2x_A = 1/2 rational, which refutes (U) outright. Conversely, (U) implies 1/2∉𝒜1/2 \notin \mathcal{A} as one instance among uncountably many, and a proof of 1/2∉𝒜1/2 \notin \mathcal{A} leaves (U) entirely open. So (H) is the maximally symmetric candidate counterexample to (U), not a restatement of it; the asymmetry is load-bearing and recurs below as Barrier . [Math]

Nothing in this document decides (U) or (H). What it does contain is (i) the unconditional record, stated with hypotheses and evidence bands, and (ii) a characterisation of the recorded attacks fail — assembled so that the failures function as measurements of one obstruction rather than as a list of disappointments.

Remark 3 (What is and is not covered in the universal direction). The pinned Lean corpus contains no theorem for A=A= the primes, but this is a formalisation boundary, not a mathematical open case: Tao and Teräväinen prove the base-22 prime-support value irrational by first identifying it with ∑n≥1ω(n)2−n\sum_{n\ge1}\omega(n)2^{-n}. The corpus still has no general theorem for an arbitrary positive-density nonperiodic or divisor-dense support, and the universal statement remains open.

The unconditional record, half-value direction

Theorem 4 (Achievement-set geometry). 𝒜\mathcal{A} is compact, closed, perfect, totally disconnected and nowhere dense, and volume⁡(𝒜)=1\operatorname{volume}(\mathcal{A}) = 1 — inside an ambient span of E≈1.6067E \approx 1.6067, a relative density of about 62%62\%. The positive-index digit coding onto 𝒜\mathcal{A} is injective: each achievable real has support. coord:achievement-set scale:uniform [Lean]
Sites: , , , , , .

Theorem 5 (Support-restricted refinement). For the achievement set built from a coordinate subset J⊆ℕJ \subseteq \mathbb{N}: either the omitted coordinate set is finite, and the volume is exactly 2−|Jc|2^{-|J^c|}, or infinitely many coordinates are omitted and the volume is 00. Injectivity survives every restriction; perfectness is proved when JJ is infinite. No perfectness claim is made for finite JJ, whose coding range is finite. coord:achievement-set scale:uniform [Lean]
Sites: , , , .

Remark 6 (Achievement-set terminology and source boundary). We use the modern term for the subsum set that Kakeya’s 1914 note describes as a set of partial sums. Kakeya proves perfectness for an absolutely convergent series and nowhere density under an all-index strict-tail condition; Kovač–Tao, Remark 4.1 verifies that strict-tail condition for the fixed-base Mersenne weights. Those sources are the classical topological antecedent. The local volume dichotomy, injectivity, and greedy-membership statements above and below are Lean-checked claims of this corpus. The sparse power-series criteria of Kaneko–Suzuki–Tachiya give neighboring sparse-support context, not a theorem about arbitrary reciprocal Mersenne subseries. [Cited]

Theorem 7 (Membership equals greedy survival; the fatal-gap dichotomy). x∈𝒜x \in \mathcal{A} iff 0≤x0 \le x and the canonical greedy (take-if-possible) residual after every rank nn satisfies ρ(x,n)≤Tn+1:=∑j>nxj\rho(x,n) \le T_{n+1} := \sum_{j > n} x_j. Unconditionally, either 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A} or a finite fatal gap exists, and the two are exactly complementary. coord:greedy-orbit scale:uniform [Lean]

Remark 8 (Literature, exactly). EE is irrational (Erdős 1948). Zudilin’s irrationality measure is μ(E)≤2.42343562…\mu(E) \le 2.42343562\ldots ( 72 (2002) 858–862; the erratum, 111 (2004) 153–164, gives 2.46497868…2.46497868\ldots). Transcendence of EE is unknown (Duverney–Tachiya, 31 (2019) 1557–1566), and the Erdős–Graham conjecture that every such subset sum is irrational — i.e. (U) — is itself open. For binary digit runs of EE the only rigorous result is a bound: Erdős constructs a 00-run of length ≥clog⁡1/10N\ge c \log^{1/10} N among the first NN bits; Crandall ( 12 (2012) #A23, §7) records the longest observed 00-run as 4747 in the first 2432^{43} bits and states that he does not know how to show that 11 appears infinitely often. Campbell (arXiv:2605.24160, 2026) settles that occurrence question affirmatively. [Cited]

That last pair of citations is the sharpest single orientation fact available. Every rigorous result in the literature about the digits of EE points the wrong way: they produce long runs, or guarantee that patterns occur. What (H) needs is that a pattern occurs for long. No result of that logical type exists.

The wall

The thesis

This programme has produced many reformulations of #257 and no proof of it. That is the honest summary, and expert readers have said so. The claim of this section is that the reformulations are not a hundred separate failures. They are repeated measurements of obstruction, taken in different coordinates, and once they are assembled the obstruction has a describable shape. A systematic elimination that says exactly which classes of argument cannot work, and why, is a result about the problem; a reformulation is not. The elimination is what follows.

The generating fact is a single structural one, and it is not a convenience of the formalisation.

Observation 9 (The problem admits no ensemble). The Mersenne weights are strictly superincreasing. Consequently the digit coding is injective (Theorem ), the greedy orbit is the unique candidate support for any target, and distinct subset sums of a row of seam weights are separated by at least 2s+12^{s+1}. Every one of the nine coordinates the corpus has built — truncation rung JJ, seam row ss, integer margin, sharp tail margin, half-carry KnK_n, reverse-carry word, Boolean–Möbius exact row, fatal-cell interval packing, Dedekind cut-locator — is therefore a coordinate on the binary digits of specific real orbit. There is no family to range over. coord:meta scale:uniform [Lean][Math]
Sites: , , .

All six barriers below are consequences of Observation  in different directions: there is nothing to choose (), nothing weaker to prove (), nothing to average over (), no information at the available scales (), no certificate in the provable direction (), and, on the universal side, no way to make a general support satisfy the certificate engine’s first hypothesis ().

Barrier 1: canonicalisation — the witness space is a singleton

Proposition 10 (Canonicalisation; proved). For the half-target in strictly superincreasing Mersenne weights, every finite object satisfying an approximate-hit condition at depth dd the canonical greedy prefix at depth dd. Precisely: (i) every straddling word at depth dd agrees bit-for-bit with the greedy support of 1/21/2 on (0,d](0,d]; (ii) every below-half core DD whose crossing deficit is smaller than the next weight is forced to equal 𝚑𝚊𝚕𝚏𝙶𝚛𝚎𝚎𝚍𝚢𝙿𝚛𝚎𝚏𝚒𝚡𝚂𝚞𝚙𝚙𝚘𝚛𝚝(c−1)\texttt{halfGreedyPrefixSupport}(c-1), so the universally quantified ∀D\forall D in the lane’s headline socket collapses onto one orbit; (iii) a remainder below the gap is equivalent to being the integer greedy bit-word. coord:straddle-prefix / integer-greedy scale:uniform [Lean]
Sites: ; ; .

Rules out. Every argument whose leverage comes from a favourable witness: a support DD, a Boolean word, a straddle prefix, an adversarial late word, or a lattice/covering configuration. At each depth the admissible set has one element, so there is no choice to exploit and no adversary to defeat.

Explains. Three recorded attack families die for exactly this reason, and their deaths look superficially unrelated. (1) proves the wrong sign: the free prefix lattice breaches the 2t/22^{t/2} safety radius in 74%74\% of t∈[8,26]t \in [8,26] — witness t=15t = 15, where fans of {2,3,5,6,10}\{2,3,5,6,10\} sum to 215+12^{15}+1, at circular distance 11; expected near-hits grow like 2t/62^{t/6}. Any generic bound on prefix cancellation therefore proves the opposite of what is wanted. [Cert]

(2) is false statically: explicit words exist at t=20t = 20 (top 1818 of 2020 bits all-11) and t=22t = 22 (top 2020 of 2222 all-00), and an unconditional construction supplies about t/12t/12 independent single-bit knobs, verified with zero exceptions to t=601t = 601. [Cert]

(3) finds nothing: zero hits, exhaustively for t≤22t \le 22 and exactly at t=40,42,45t = 40, 42, 45 over all cut positions. [Cert]

The reconciliation is the content: residues mod 2t2^t are adversary-tunable, but the integer is not, because the row weights are gap-dominated. So the static tier and the dynamic tier coincide identically, and all three families were, without knowing it, measuring the same single orbit.

Remark 11 (A recorded hazard). The natural sufficient condition via fractional split-mass is necessary on real crossing cores: the fixture D={2,3}D = \{2,3\}, c=5c = 5 is an explicit counterexample (). Any attack on the capacity socket that routes through fractional mass is already refuted. [Lean]

The extra quantifier buys nothing. The mechanism is a single exact identity plus a single unconditional envelope.

Barrier 3: scale mismatch — the available information is at the wrong resolution

The input the half-value branch actually needs is a per-index, growing-precision, near-integer anti-concentration bound: at reset row rr, a lower bound on the distance from ℤ\mathbb{Z} of ∑i≤Lδ(M+i)2−i\sum_{i \le L} \delta(M+i)\,2^{-i} with δ(M)=τ(M)−1\delta(M) = \tau(M) - 1, where the precision demanded grows like 2−r/22^{-r/2} while the window length is only L≈r/2L \approx r/2. Every information source tried lives at one of two extremes, and provably cannot reach that intermediate scale.

Class (a): fixed precision or bounded state. Three landed theorems, all problem-agnostic — they mention no Mersenne structure and bind #249 identically.

(ii) No bounded or autonomous state summarising the history before position mm determines the tail after mm: for a balanced-pulse family no decoder recovers the radius, and any finite state type needs cardinality at least ⌊m/2⌋+2\lfloor m/2 \rfloor + 2, unbounded in mm (). (iii) For any starting carry and any finite word of odd valuation-unit symbols at fixed precision u>0u > 0, a compatible centred carry completion (), so fixed-precision local data never excludes anything. coord:carry scale:uniform [Lean]

The parity route is the same fact by hand: “K(M)K(M) even ⇔\iff MM a perfect square” is true, but J(M+1)=2J(M)−δ(M+1)J(M+1) = 2J(M) - \delta(M+1) makes J(M+1)≡δ(M+1)(mod⁡2)J(M+1) \equiv \delta(M+1) \pmod 2 an identity for digit stream whatsoever. It is a tautology of the recursion shape; it forbids no residue and no run. [Math]

Class (b): global averages and Diophantine data.

Proposition 17 (Exponent-budget mismatch; proved, given a cited μ\mu). The skip set at row nn has |Skipn|≈n2/4|\mathrm{Skip}_n| \approx n^2/4, so an irrationality-measure exponent μ\mu for the target constant yields a separation of order only 2−μn2/42^{-\mu n^2/4}, while the required precision is 2−3n/22^{-3n/2}. The shortfall is a factor ≈0.42n\approx 0.42\,n , and it grows linearly in nn. Since μ≥2\mu \ge 2 for every irrational, no improvement in μ\mu can close it: Zudilin’s μ(E)≤2.42343562…\mu(E) \le 2.42343562\ldots is irrelevant to the gap, and so is any future bound. coord:diophantine scale:cofinal [Math][Cited]

Rules out. Any argument deriving the run-length or magnitude bound from (a) arithmetic information at fixed finite precision or a bounded automaton state, or (b) a global average, density, or Diophantine-approximation quantity attached to C=E−3/2C = E - 3/2. Concretely: no proposal to bound the R-run via an irrationality measure of a Mersenne or Erdős–Borwein-type constant can work, however good the measure becomes; and no proposal defining a bounded carry state summarising pre-index history can determine the post-index tail.

Explains. Prime-doubling fails for a recorded reason rather than for want of effort: NN prime ≥n\ge n gives b(N)=1b(N) = 1 so JJ doubles at that step, but not cumulatively, because composites subtract. The explicit witness is the quiet run at n=607n = 607, spanning M∈(607,617]M \in (607,617] with J∈[1,5]J \in [1,5] for eleven steps ; and 2626 of the 4040 longest runs with n≤1500n \le 1500 contain a prime. No run-length bound follows from prime counting. [Cert]

Remark 18 (Status of the exhaustion claim). The seven named families are each closed with mechanism. The claim that classes (a) and (b) the available tools is an observed pattern, not a theorem, and is labelled as such wherever it is used below.

Barrier 4: decision asymmetry — the certificates point the wrong way

Theorem 19 (One-sidedness; proved). 1/2∉𝒜1/2 \notin \mathcal{A} is Σ10\Sigma^0_1: a single finite object — a fatal gap — certifies it. 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A} is Π10\Pi^0_1, and no finite object certifies it. Consequently no finite computation, at any depth, can establish 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A}. coord:meta scale:uniform [Lean]

Proof. The dichotomy 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A} or ∃\exists a fatal gap is unconditional (), and the two alternatives are exactly complementary (), with a finite witness type. In the other direction, certified death implies non-membership (, over ; 3/43/4 is certified dead at level 11, lookahead 00, by ), whereas the absence of such a certificate at any depth DD is compatible with a certificate at depth D+1D+1 and therefore proves nothing. Membership asserts survival at rank (Theorem ), an infinite conjunction with no finite sub-conjunction implying it. ◻

Rules out. Any programme whose plan is “extend the certified depth”. Pushing the truncation rung to J=23J = 23, the seam to row 10610^6, or the macro receipt to depth 10810^8 cannot in principle decide the branch — each raises a lower bound on a death rank which, if the supported branch is correct, does not exist.

Explains. Every certificate the programme owns is of this one type. The certified depths grew by roughly two orders of magnitude across the recorded history with no change whatsoever in decision status; that is not a coincidence to be pushed through, it is the theorem above being observed empirically. Accumulated survival is not convergence toward proof.

Barrier 5: measure and category point in opposite directions

Proposition 20 (The two soft heuristics contradict each other; proved). 𝒜\mathcal{A} has Lebesgue measure exactly 11 inside an ambient span of E≈1.6067E \approx 1.6067, a relative density of about 62%62\%, and is simultaneously nowhere dense, perfect and totally disconnected (Theorem ). Hence the measure heuristic — “a random point lies in 𝒜\mathcal{A} with probability ≈0.62\approx 0.62” — predicts #257 , while the category heuristic — “𝒜\mathcal{A} is meagre, so a generic point misses it” — predicts #257 . coord:achievement-set scale:uniform [Lean]

Rules out. Every soft argument: measure-theoretic, Baire-category, metric number theory (almost-all / almost-none), and probabilistic digit models. The two standard notions of “typical” disagree on this object, so neither can be the mechanism. Worse, by injectivity of the digit coding (Observation ) there is no ensemble of candidate representations to average over: each rational has exactly one candidate support, so counting, second-moment and pigeonhole arguments have nothing to range over. It also rules out deciding (U) by showing 𝒜\mathcal{A} is “small”: it is not small — it is 62%62\% of its ambient interval by measure.

Explains. The programme’s own probabilistic estimate sits squarely on the losing side of this split: under a Bernoulli(1/2)(1/2) digit model the expected number of counterexamples with n≥32n \ge 32 is about 2×10−42 \times 10^{-4}, i.e. the model predicts 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A}. That estimate is worth exactly as much as the model, and the model is a measure-side object that cannot see a specific point of a nowhere-dense set having Lebesgue measure exactly 11. [Cert]

Barrier 6: the two-axis certificate box (universal direction)

Observation 21 (The box; observed pattern). Every landed unconditional theorem in the table of § requires the support to sit inside a two-axis box: (i) divisor independence, so that a CRT construction can prescribe the incidence sc⁡A\operatorname{sc}_A across a block — pairwise coprimality, periodicity, or dilation of a full support; and (ii) a global tail budget, so that the middle window’s mass satisfies the height inequality q(C+N+L+2)<bLq(C+N+L+2) < b^L — summable reciprocals, or sparsity that makes this trivial. No landed theorem sits outside the box. This is a complete audit of the landed inventory, not a theorem that no such support can exist. coord:certificate-engine scale:uniform [Lean][Math]

Rules out. Any plan to obtain (U) by instantiating the existing engine at a general infinite AA. For a general support the divisibility conditions a∣na \mid n, a∈Aa \in A, are through pairwise gcds, so no CRT construction can prescribe the incidence in a block, and the engine’s first hypothesis is unsatisfiable by construction rather than by search failure. It also rules out closing the gap by “removing the summability bound” from Erdős 1968: the bound is consumed at exactly one step, CertificateKernel.lean:9586--9598, as a global tail budget. Removing it is not weakening a hypothesis; it requires a different, windowed argument.

Explains only a method boundary. The primes are infinite and pairwise coprime — axis (i) is satisfied in the cleanest possible way, and makes the dilation algebra exact there — yet this certificate theorem does not apply because ∑1/p\sum1/p diverges by Mertens and axis (ii) fails. This explains the absence of a ; it does not make the base-22 value open, since Tao–Teräväinen settle it by a different analytic method. The sunflower generalisation inherits both axes and therefore does not recover that external theorem.

What the six barriers converge on

Both halves of #257 terminate at the same missing object, stated twice in two coordinates. On the half-value side it is a near-integer anti-concentration bound for ∑i≤L(τ(M+i)−1)2−i\sum_{i \le L} (\tau(M+i) - 1)\,2^{-i}, a geometrically weighted divisor sum in a short interval. On the universal side it is the dense-branch producer: for a divisor-dense AA, a block of KK consecutive indices with 2K∣∑r=1Ksc⁡A(N+r)2K−r2^K \mid \sum_{r=1}^{K} \operatorname{sc}_A(N+r)\,2^{K-r} and a bounded middle window. These are the same statement in the incidence coordinate. No result of that shape exists in the literature in any form, and the only rigorous results in that direction — lower bounds on runs, and guarantees that patterns occur — have the opposite logical type. That convergence, from two independent directions, is the strongest evidence the corpus offers that there is exactly one wall here rather than several.

What the wall does not block

Six barriers eliminate a great deal. What they do not eliminate is a short, specific list, and the point of the elimination is that this list is short. Each route below is given with the exact statement it needs, the barrier it evades, and it evades it. Where a route evades every proved barrier but sits inside the class indicted by an observed pattern, that is said plainly.

Ranking, stated plainly

Route 4 is the only one that can be completed with the mathematics currently in hand; it produces theorems, not progress on the wall. Route 3 is the only one that would produce a new irrationality theorem for a named constant, and its missing input is a windowed Mertens estimate, which is ordinary analytic number theory rather than a new phenomenon. Route 2 is the only place in the half-value branch with a non-singleton witness space, which makes it the best target for search. Route 1 is where the actual obstruction lives, and Route 5 is Route 1 in another coordinate. Neither problem is close to being solved, and no route above is a proof of anything.

Reading the detailed record

The opening note has already defined the evidence bands, scale tags, coordinates, and catalogue terminology. The longer record has two different reading modes, and they should not be confused.

Read linearly.

Sections  and form one argument: the first identifies the recurring obstructions, and the second isolates the routes those obstructions do not exclude. Read them in order before selecting a new attack.

Use as reference.

The mathematical-ingredient catalogue may be entered by coordinate: the certificate method and universal-direction record; the greedy and achievement-set geometry; the seam model, master identity, and dynamics; the half-carry and Boolean–Möbius coordinates; and the support rigidity results. The later implication tables record what chains with what, while the near-miss index gives the exact mismatch at each open obligation.

Scale and coordinate discipline.

The direct certified instances remain fixed or bounded — rungs J≤22J \le 22, seam rows ≤200,000\le 200{,}000, ranks ≤3000\le 3000, and macro depth ≤13,548,057\le 13{,}548{,}057 — whereas the open obligations are cofinal. Theorem  shows that extending a bounded range does not establish a cofinal statement. Coordinate tags are equally literal: an obstruction in coord:half-carry, coord:seam-row, or coord:diophantine does not transfer to another representation without a proved map. Coordinate-free barriers are marked explicitly.

The object, the two questions, and the exact record

The object

Fix the Mersenne weight function xn:=1/(2n−1)x_n := 1/(2^n-1) for integers n≥2n \ge 2. For a set A⊆{2,3,4,…}A \subseteq \{2,3,4,\dots\}, write xA:=∑n∈Axnx_A := \sum_{n \in A} x_n when the sum converges (it always does, since xn=O(2−n)x_n = O(2^{-n})). Erdős’s Problem #257 asks about the family of series {xA:A infinite}\{x_A : A \text{ infinite}\}.

Definition 22 (Universal Problem #257). Is xA=∑n∈A1/(2n−1)x_A = \sum_{n \in A} 1/(2^n-1) irrational for infinite A⊆ℕA \subseteq \mathbb{N}? This is a single universally-quantified statement over all infinite subsets of ℕ\mathbb{N}. It is OPEN. [Open]

The record in this paper does decide universal #257. Everything that follows is either (i) a proof of irrationality for specific, named infinite-support families – which narrows but does not close the universal statement, since infinitely many other supports remain unchecked – or (ii) an attack on one specific, maximally symmetric candidate counterexample, described next.

Definition 23 (The distinguished half-value question). Define the 𝒜:={y∈ℝ:∃A⊆ℕ,0∉A,y=∑n∈Axn}\mathcal{A} := \{\,y \in \mathbb{R} : \exists A \subseteq \mathbb{N},\ 0 \notin A,\ y = \sum_{n \in A} x_n\,\}, the set of reals realizable as a subset sum of the positive-index Mersenne weights {xn}n≥1\{x_n\}_{n \ge 1}. Is 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A}? This is OPEN. [Open]

Observation 24 (Why the half-value question controls universal #257). Any finite subset sum of {xn}\{x_n\} has odd reduced denominator, since every 2n−12^n - 1 is odd; hence no finite AA can sum to 1/21/2 (). Consequently, 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A}, the witnessing support AA is necessarily infinite, and xA=1/2x_A = 1/2 is rational. Such an AA is then a single infinite set for which the universal-#257 sum is rational – an outright refutation of universal #257. Conversely, universal #257 being true forces 1/2∉𝒜1/2 \notin \mathcal{A} as one instance among uncountably many. The half-value question is thus the maximally symmetric, most heavily studied test case for universal #257’s negation, not a restatement of it: proving 1/2∉𝒜1/2 \notin \mathcal{A} leaves universal #257 completely open (all other infinite AA remain unchecked), while proving 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A} closes universal #257 immediately, in the negative. scale:n/a [Math]

What is proved

Full-support irrationality, for every base

Theorem 25 (Full-support irrationality, unconditional, every base b≥2b \ge 2). For every integer b≥2b \ge 2, ∑k=0∞1bk+1−1is irrational.\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{b^{k+1}-1} \quad \text{is irrational.} Hypotheses: b∈ℕb \in \mathbb{N}, b≥2b \ge 2. Conclusion: unconditional irrationality of the full-support Erdős–Borwein-type series at every base, not merely base 22. coord:full-support scale:uniform [Lean]

This is the base-bb generalization of Erdős’s original 1948 irrationality theorem for ∑1/(2n−1)\sum 1/(2^n-1) (cited, in its base-22 form, as an input at Remark  below); its Lean form removes the base restriction entirely and is landed with no open hypotheses.

The greedy orbit, exactly

Fix the target 1/21/2 and the weights xn=1/(2n−1)x_n = 1/(2^n-1), n≥2n \ge 2 (rank 11 contributes the undefined x1x_1 and is excluded by convention; all indexing below starts at rank 22). The greedy orbit is the unique deterministic process forced by superincreasingness (Theorem ):

Definition 32 (The half-value greedy orbit). Let ρ1:=1/2\rho_1 := 1/2 (the residual entering rank 22). At rank k≥2k \ge 2, given residual ρk\rho_k:

  • Take iff ρk≥xk\rho_k \ge x_k; if taken, ρk+1:=ρk−xk\rho_{k+1} := \rho_k - x_k.

  • Skip otherwise; ρk+1:=ρk\rho_{k+1} := \rho_k.

A skip at rank kk is:

  • safe iff ρk≤Tk+1:=∑j>kxj\rho_k \le T_{k+1} := \sum_{j>k} x_j (the residual still fits inside the remaining tail, so future ranks can still reach it);

  • fatal iff ρk∈(Tk+1,xk)\rho_k \in (T_{k+1}, x_k) (the residual is too large for the remaining tail to ever reach, yet too small to have been taken at kk – an impossible gap).

By Theorem , 1/2∈𝒜1/2 \in \mathcal{A} iff no rank of this orbit is ever fatal. Two boundary degeneracies are excluded unconditionally and independently of any open hypothesis:

Remark 33 (No-ties: both greedy-orbit boundaries are strict). (a) ρk≠xk\rho_k \ne x_k at any rank: a finite Mersenne sum has odd reduced denominator (each 2n−12^n-1 is odd), so no finite prefix mass can equal xkx_k exactly, sharpening the general denominator-parity fact used in Observation . (b) ρk≠Tk+1\rho_k \ne T_{k+1} at any rank: the tail Tk+1=E−1−∑2≤j≤kxjT_{k+1} = E - 1 - \sum_{2 \le j \le k} x_j, where E:=∑n≥1xnE := \sum_{n\ge1} x_n is the Erdős–Borwein constant, is irrational by Erdős’s own 1948 theorem (the base-22 case of Theorem ), while ρk\rho_k is always rational; equality is impossible. Conclusion: both greedy-orbit boundaries are provably strict at every rank, so the orbit’s decisions stabilize after finitely many strict inequalities at any fixed truncation depth. coord:no-ties scale:uniform [Math]

The seam model and the master identity

The seam model is a base-44 rescaled integer reformulation of Definition , built so that every quantity involved is an exact natural number (no real-number or limiting arithmetic). Fix a row n≥6n \ge 6. The seam weights at row nn are w(n,d):=⌊4n2d−1⌋,d=2,…,n−1,w(n,d) := \left\lfloor \frac{4^n}{2^d-1} \right\rfloor, \qquad d = 2,\dots,n-1, and the seam target is Tn:=22n−1−2nT_n := 2^{2n-1} - 2^n. The seam greedy process takes ranks d=2,…,n−1d = 2,\dots,n-1 in ascending order against TnT_n exactly as in Definition , producing a take set Dn⊆{2,…,n−1}D_n \subseteq \{2,\dots,n-1\} and skip set Skipn:={2,…,n−1}∖Dn\mathrm{Skip}_n := \{2,\dots,n-1\} \mathbin{\backslash} D_n. Catalogue of mathematical ingredients

This section catalogues machinery for Erdős #257 (is ∑n∈A1/(2n−1)\sum_{n\in A} 1/(2^n-1) irrational for every infinite A⊆ℕA\subseteq\mathbb{N}?) drawn from the half-membership route (is 1/21/2 in the Mersenne achievement set?) and the support-rigidity / full-support route (irrationality of ∑a∈A1/(2a−1)\sum_{a\in A} 1/(2^a-1) for named families AA). Every entry states exact hypotheses, exact conclusion, coordinate, scale, evidence band, and Lean site. Nothing below decides #257; the problem remains open. Entries are grouped Producers (hypothesis ⇒\Rightarrow conclusion, including conditional sockets whose hypothesis is itself an open sub-obligation, always flagged) and Converters and exact identities (iff-reformulations, structural invariants, definitions, exact numerals). Within each subsection entries are ordered by scale: fixed << bounded << cofinal << uniform << n/a.

Theorem 41 (Cofinal skip forces half-membership). Fatality is absorbing for the greedy Mersenne recursion at target x≥0x\ge 0: once holds it holds at every n+kn+k, and forces every later exponent selected, so a fatal state leaves only finitely many omitted exponents. Contrapositively: if the greedy skipped support (the set of ranks the greedy process does select) is infinite, then xx lies in the Mersenne achievement set.

Consequence theorems

The BooleanMöbius lane (repo root Erdos257PeriodNoncollapse/, mirrored at Erdos249257/ for the modules that have been made public) is where the reduction of Erdős #257 to a single arithmetic socket actually lives. Sixteen of its modules have never been published: BooleanMobiusCofinalExactRows, BooleanMobiusCriticalCapacityCofinal, BooleanMobiusCriticalCapacityGeometric, BooleanMobiusExactRowCrossing, BooleanMobiusExactRowDichotomy, BooleanMobiusExactRowDoubling, BooleanMobiusExactRowRankTwo, BooleanMobiusExactRowSeed, BooleanMobiusExactTransition, BooleanMobiusGlobalRepair, BooleanMobiusGreedyReduction, BooleanMobiusLocalRepair, BooleanMobiusSkipRow, BooleanMobiusSkipRowCofinal, BooleanMobiusSkippedCoreCriticalCapacity, BooleanMobiusSkippedCoreExactRow; plus three sibling modules on the half-membership track, also never published: HalfGapMass, HalfGreedyFatalGap, HalfUpperResetCriticalBand. Every one of the nineteen is covered below. Consumers in this subsection are theorems whose conclusion is a genuine payoff ((1/2:ℝ)∈mersenneAchievementSet(1/2:\mathbb{R})\in\mathrm{mersenneAchievementSet}, or an infinite counterexample support) but whose hypothesis is an unsupplied predicate. Every such hypothesis is displayed, not buried in prose: that predicate is the actual target.

The load-bearing definitions

Definition 103 (257bm:d1 — ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow). For n:ℕn:\mathbb{N}: ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow(n):=∃D:Finsetℕ,(∀d∈D,2≤d≤n)∧localPrefixQuotient(D,n)=2n−1−1.\mathrm{ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow}(n) \;:=\; \exists D:\mathrm{Finset}\,\mathbb{N},\ (\forall d\in D,\ 2\le d\le n) \ \wedge\ \mathrm{localPrefixQuotient}(D,n) = 2^{n-1}-1 . A finite Boolean support DD bounded by nn exactly hits the integer target 2n−1−12^{n-1}-1 under floor-division Mersenne quotients at scale nn — the natural-number carry accounting is exact, not merely close.

Definition 106 (257bm:d4 — CofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows, THE MASTER PREMISE). CofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows:=∀N:ℕ,∃n:ℕ,N≤n∧ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow(n).\mathrm{CofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows} \;:=\; \forall N:\mathbb{N},\ \exists n:\mathbb{N},\ N\le n\ \wedge\ \mathrm{ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow}(n). This weakening is simultaneously the whole reason the lane is tractable and the exact place an attacker must be careful: a proof that looks like it supplies coherent rows is doing strictly more work than is needed, and a proof that looks like it refutes coherent rows says nothing about this predicate.

Invariants are unconditional identities, monotonicity facts, and quantitative bounds that hold regardless of which branch of the lane’s case splits fires. They are the load-bearing algebra every producer and consumer above is built from.

Greedy-window uniqueness (BooleanMobiusGreedyReduction)

Theorem 140 (257bm:i11a — remainder_lt_gap_iff_eq_integerGreedyBits). Under gap dominance (the next digit’s weight strictly exceeds the sum of all lower digits’ slack), a Boolean word matches the unique greedy-bit word IFF its remainder is below the separation gap. Whenever the separation gap dominates there is exactly ONE admissible Boolean word achieving a given target defect — the greedy word. The "superincreasing weight sequence ++ below-gap remainder ⇒\Rightarrow unique greedy word" technique is standard and fully general, independent of the Mersenne instantiation.

Obstructions and countermodels

Every record below is a HAZARD RECORD: a proof that some plausible-looking route to cofinality, either does not work, or provably cannot work as stated. These are load-bearing warnings, not merely negative curiosities — several are the exact reason the corpus’s live attack is aimed where it is aimed, and re-deriving what they already kill wastes a proof attempt.

Theorem 167 (257bm:k1 — boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel_not_cofinal, THE DICHOTOMY-SHAPE FALSIFIER — read before re-deriving cofinality from the dichotomy alone). The dichotomy ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow(2n−1)∨∃c,4≤c≤n∧ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow(2c−2)\mathrm{ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow}(2n{-}1) \vee \exists c,\,4\le c\le n\wedge \mathrm{ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow}(2c{-}2) (proved for n≥6n\ge6 at 257bm:k-dich below) is not by itself enough for cofinality. Countermodel: boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel(n):=(n=6)\mathrm{boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel}(n) := (n=6) satisfies EXACTLY the same two-branch transition shape (seed at 6, and boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel_transition reproduces the ∨\vee shape by always taking the recycle branch with c=4c=4, landing back at 2⋅4−2=62\cdot4-2=6), yet ¬(∀N,∃n≥N,boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel(n))(NOT cofinal — only ever true at n=6).\neg\big(\forall N,\ \exists n\ge N,\ \mathrm{boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel}(n)\big) \qquad \text{(NOT cofinal — only ever true at } n=6\text{)}. Packaged existentially as exists_seeded_bounded_double_or_recycle_model. The double-or-recycle transition shape, EVEN TOGETHER with an endpoint-six seed, is logically insufficient to conclude cofinal exact rows. A genuinely new progress input (strict endpoint growth, or an independent cofinality argument) is required. The TECHNIQUE — build a bounded one-point fixed model with the same recursion shape to show a transition schema doesn’t imply cofinality — is fully general and transfers to any other double-or-recycle-shaped inductive scheme, including one built for #249.

The scale ladder

Every claim in this programme carries a tag alongside its evidence band. The two axes are independent and both matter to a reader deciding whether a result can be used as a premise. Evidence answers “is this checked, and how”: [Lean] is kernel-checked in the live Lean tree, [Cert] is an exact finite computation (integer arithmetic, no floating point, often independently reproduced), [Math] is ordinary mathematics carried out in prose and checked by a human or an adversarial audit pass but not yet formalised, [Cited] invokes a published external theorem, and [Open] marks an unproved hypothesis that some consumer theorem is conditioned on.

Scale answers a different question, “over how much of the problem does this claim range”: scale:fixed is one concrete numeral or witness; scale:bounded produces a witness whose size is controlled by the input (typically ≤n\le n for input nn); scale:uniform holds unconditionally for every nn above an explicit threshold, with no existential slack; scale:cofinal asserts ∀N∃n≥N,…\forall N\,\exists n\ge N,\ldots — infinitely many witnesses, arbitrarily far out, with coherence required between them. scale:n/a tags definitions and other scale-free statements.

Scale is the load-bearing axis of the whole corpus. Both open problems are, at bottom, cofinal statements: #257 half-membership needs infinitely many exact rows or infinitely many positive greedy skips (Table , rows C1/C3), and the unconditional track needs a run-length bound that holds at every reset row out to infinity, not merely to a certified depth. Every machine-checked theorem in the tree is fixed, bounded, or uniform. No amount of raising a uniform certificate’s threshold, by itself, produces a cofinal witness — a uniform statement “∀n≥N0\forall n\ge N_0” is a single first-order sentence with no existential content past N0N_0, while a cofinal statement needs infinitely many , which is a strictly different logical shape.

Table  samples the ladder across all four non-trivial scales, drawn from the BooleanMobius, HalfCutLocator, GreedyAchievementSet, and seam-integer (HalfCylinder*) families together with the truncation-rung ladder and the sign/irrationality primitives that feed all of them. The horizontal rule marks the frontier: everything above it is proved (fixed, bounded, or uniform); everything below it is what the open producers still need (cofinal), stated with its exact quantifier prefix so the gap is visible, not merely asserted.

Remark 187 (Nothing promotes for free). A natural question, once the ladder is visible, is whether any scale:uniform or scale:bounded result already in the tree secretly the cofinal statement in disguise — whether some existing theorem’s hypothesis, read carefully enough, is uniform in a parameter that a cofinal witness sequence could simply walk through. An audit pass read each Lean proof body (not just the statement) of eighteen such candidates drawn from the fixed/bounded/uniform rows of Table  and their immediate neighbours, checking specifically for a proof technique general enough to instantiate at an unboundedly growing parameter without degradation.

None promoted. The recurring blockers were three: a finite certificate table baked into the proof (the bound only extends as far as the table was built, rows 13–31 in ); a kernel interval_cases/decide discharge over an explicitly bounded range, which is definitionally not re-runnable past its stated bound; and constants inside the bound that degrade with the very parameter a cofinal witness would need to grow (a threshold of the shape 2(r+5)/22^{(r+5)/2} or a margin that shrinks as 1/N1/\sqrt N is uniform any fixed depth but does not, by itself, manufacture the next witness at a larger depth).

This is consistent with, not a substitute for, the general logical point above: promoting a uniform statement to a cofinal one requires new content — an explicit witness-producing construction — not a change of quantifier bookkeeping.

One orbit in four coordinates

One decision stream, four integerisations

Fix the weights xn:=1/(2n−1)x_n:=1/(2^n-1), n≥2n\ge2, and the target 1/21/2. A skip at rank kk is iff ρ≤Tk+1:=∑j>kxj\rho\le T_{k+1}:=\sum_{j>k}x_j and iff ρ∈(Tk+1,xk)\rho\in(T_{k+1},x_k) — the fatal interval is exactly the gap no later tail can repair. The rank-by-rank take/skip margin against the exact tail, checked for ranks 22 through 30003000: 14971497 takes against 15021502 skips, zero fatal skips anywhere, minimum certified gap-margin +2.9922+2.9922 bits at rank 55, and the single tightest real data point in the whole corpus at rank 77 — the near-tie 1/126≥1/1271/126\ge1/127, margin +0.0340+0.0340 bits (source: erdos257_reset_crossing_unification_2026_07_24.md, §8).

Proposition 188 (One orbit, four coordinates). Fix the weights xn=1/(2n−1)x_n=1/(2^n-1) and target 1/21/2. Sufficiently fine truncations of any one of the four integerisations above reproduce the full greedy orbit’s decisions exactly on any fixed finite prefix of ranks; consequently all four coordinates decide the question, namely whether 1/21/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set.

Mechanism. This is not an approximation claim to be taken on faith; it rests on the fact below. ◻

Lemma 189 (No-ties lemma). At every rank kk of the full greedy orbit for target 1/21/2, both defining comparisons are strict: ρ≠xk\rho\ne x_k and ρ≠Tk+1\rho\ne T_{k+1}.

Proof. Two independent mechanisms, one for each boundary, both closing a boundary that a naive truncation argument would otherwise have to worry about degenerating on.

Any finite Mersenne sum P/D:=∑d∈DxdP/D:=\sum_{d\in D}x_d has DD odd, since every weight’s denominator 2d−12^d-1 is odd and a product/lcm of odd numbers is odd (equivalently, , itself traced to ). Hence the residual after any finite prefix is ρ=12−PD=D−2P2D\rho=\tfrac12-\tfrac{P}{D}=\tfrac{D-2P}{2D}: its reduced denominator is . Every weight xk=1/(2k−1)x_k=1/(2^k-1) has denominator. An even-denominator rational can never equal an odd-denominator rational, so ρ=xk\rho=x_k is impossible at any rank — the take comparison is never a tie.

The tail past rank kk is Tk+1=E−1−∑2≤j≤kxjT_{k+1}=E-1-\sum_{2\le j\le k}x_j, where E=∑n≥11/(2n−1)E=\sum_{n\ge1}1/(2^n-1) is the Erdős–Borwein constant: a rational shift of EE. Erdős’s own 1948 theorem gives EE irrational (, instantiated at b=2b=2), so Tk+1T_{k+1} is irrational for every kk. The residual ρ\rho arising from any finite Boolean prefix is rational. An irrational number never equals a rational one, so ρ=Tk+1\rho=T_{k+1} is impossible at any rank — the skip-safety comparison is never a tie either.

Both boundaries of the fatal interval (Tk+1,xk)(T_{k+1},x_k) are therefore approached only strictly, at every rank, unconditionally. 0◻ ◻

Remark 190. Lemma  is exactly what licenses Proposition : because no comparison is ever exactly on a boundary, every rank’s decision is stable under sufficiently fine truncation — there is no knife-edge case where refining JJ, extending ss, tightening mcm_c, or sharpening the tail margin could flip a decision that a coarser coordinate had already settled on a fixed prefix. This is the sense in which the four bullet points above are one decision stream, not four independent producers that happen to agree so far.

Frontier index: what stands between the corpus and a proof

This section is the sharp end of the paper. Parts I–II assembled the corpus; here every result in it is tested against three exact open obligations and rendered as a usable premise: what it yields, the exact mismatch against the obligation, a classified gap kind (hypothesis_strength, scale_only, quantifier_order, coordinate_only, or multiple), and the exact auxiliary statement that would close it. Nothing here decides #249 or #257; the corpus’s own moderator standard applies throughout — a reduction is not a result, and a finite verified list is not a cofinal supply.

The three #257 obligations, stated exactly

Definition 198 (257-reset). For every reset row r≥31r \ge 31: Δr+12>2r+5\Delta_{r+1}^2 > 2^{r+5}, where Δr+1\Delta_{r+1} is the signed deviation of the greedy remainder from 2r+12^{r+1} at the row immediately following reset rr. Equivalently: the R-run (all-right run) beginning at reset rr has length Lr<(r−3)/2L_r < (r-3)/2. Equivalently, at the natural dyadic scale 2−n2^{-n}, the greedy skip-set sum never approximates C=E−3/2C = E - 3/2 to within about 2−1.5n2^{-1.5n} (here EE is the Erdős–Borwein constant). Any bound Lr=o(r)L_r = o(r) closes the obligation. A constant bound on LrL_r is FALSE — runs grow like log⁡2(row)\log_2(\mathrm{row}) — so the correct target is a growing, not constant, run-length ceiling.

Definition 199 (257-cofinal-rows). ∀N∃n≥N\forall N\ \exists n \ge N with nn — i.e. cofinally many finite prefixes whose local Mersenne quotient lands exactly on the half-value residue class. Consumed unconditionally by . No coherence between the witnessing rows is demanded and none should be assumed: the rows may be, and in the corpus’s own words, mutually incompatible — only their endpoint lengths need tend to infinity. Any weakening that reintroduces a compatibility requirement between rows is not a weakening of this obligation; it is a different, harder one.

Definition 200 (257-universal). ∀b≥2∀A⊆ℕ\forall b \ge 2\ \forall A \subseteq \mathbb{N} infinite: ∑n∈A1/(bn−1)\sum_{n \in A} 1/(b^n-1) is irrational. This is Erdős #257 at full strength — every infinite support, not one target value and not one structural class.

Reading a row

Each entry below has the form: tag — declarations, site (file:line, opened and read, not inferred), gap_kind, yields (the exact statement, quantifiers preserved), mismatch (the precise distance from the obligation, with the mechanism), closes (the exact auxiliary statement — not a vague direction — that would discharge the row). Evidence band is [Lean] unless marked [Math] or [Cert] (exact finite computation).

257-reset: sixteen near misses

Observation 201 (oa-2 / deficit-side run law). [Lean] . Yields: ∀k,s.5≤s→rem(s)≤2s→2s≤2k(2s−rem(s))→∃t∈[s,s+k]\forall k, s.\ 5 \le s \to \mathrm{rem}(s) \le 2^s \to 2^s \le 2^k(2^s - \mathrm{rem}(s)) \to \exists t \in [s,s+k] with an upper-or-middle event at tt. The only unconditional deficit bound on hand is integrality (rem(s)<2s⇒\mathrm{rem}(s) < 2^s \Rightarrow deficit ≥1\ge 1); instantiating k=sk=s with deficit ≥20\ge 2^0 gives only Lr≤rL_r \le r. The obligation needs Lr<(r−3)/2L_r < (r-3)/2 — short by exactly a factor of two in the exponent. Closes it: 2(r+3)/2≤2r−rem(r)2^{(r+3)/2} \le 2^r - \mathrm{rem}(r) at every reset r≥31r \ge 31. Three theorems assembled from the interface, and where each still stops

[Math] throughout this subsection — none of Theorems A, B, C is a Lean declaration. Each is a correct assembly of the corpus’s proved pieces plus one clearly named open step; none decides #257.

Theorem 243 (A — reset-crossing unification). The 257-reset target exponent (r+5)/2(r+5)/2 is not a fitted constant but a one: it follows from sqrt-scale reset anti-concentration together with the run-length-to-crossing geometry of oa-2’s deficit/excess pair above, and every correction constant in the derivation is exact (no asymptotic O(⋅)O(\cdot) notation is hiding a table). Concretely: the deficit-side run law (oa-2, unconditional and uniform) converts any anti-concentration bound 2εr2^{\varepsilon r} on |Δr||\Delta_r| into a run-length ceiling Lr≲(1−ε)⋅2rL_r \lesssim (1-\varepsilon)\cdot 2r; matching this against the certified maximum observed run growth (SE-7: max⁡Lr∼log⁡2(row)\max L_r \sim \log_2(\mathrm{row}), row 200,000) pins ε=1/2\varepsilon = 1/2 as the exact crossover exponent, not merely a plausible guess. Theorem A is the unification of the deficit-run and excess-run geometry into one crossing socket at that derived exponent; the open step is exactly the anti-concentration input identified in the G5/H4/F5b/oa-3b rows above.

Theorem 244 (B — rigidity of dangerous resets). A dangerous reset (one within 2(r+5)/22^{(r+5)/2} of the sqrt-escape threshold) that is preceded by a long pure R-run pins its own deviation to a single pulse-determined integer (RC-5 above), not a free real number: the affine excess recurrence (rc-2) is exact, so once the run length and the pulse word are fixed, wr0+1w_{r_0+1} is one of at most two integers with no remaining degree of freedom. Consequently a chain of nn dangerous resets is not nn independent near-misses; it is a single tower of n−1n{-}1 nested exact integer coincidences, each individually as unlikely as an explicit arithmetic accident and none free to vary once the pulse stream is fixed. Failure of sqrt-escape therefore requires an exact integer-coincidence tower, not a generic accumulation of small errors — the open step is excluding the two pinned values (RC-5’s own closing condition).

Theorem 245 (C — the one-sided finite decision boundary). The checked equivalence separates two logically different kinds of evidence. A fatal greedy gap found at a finite rank is a finite certificate that 1/2∉𝒜1/2\notin\mathcal A. By contrast, membership requires survival at every rank; the corpus supplies no finite certificate that the orbit survives forever and no completion theorem turning a long surviving prefix into membership.

The reset-crossing sockets, truncation-rung ladder, and sharp-capacity inequalities feed sufficient conditions for a finite fatal gap. They are not proved equivalent to one another, nor is failure to find one at a given depth evidence of survival. Consequently these searches give at most a semi-decision procedure for . Halting does not prove the universal statement in #257, and non-halting does not prove that 1/21/2 is represented. In particular, neither truth nor falsity of the universal problem is shown semi-decidable here. Deeper negative search alone establishes nothing beyond the tested finite ranks; this is the quantifier boundary recorded by SE-7/RC-7.

Route-collapse findings: four traps to name explicitly

These four rows are not near-misses to be closed by further work — they are targets that, once adversarially checked, turn out to be logically equivalent to the obligation itself (or to 1/2∈mersenneAchievementSet1/2\in\mathrm{mersenneAchievementSet} directly) for the scope in which they are stated. Treating any of them as an easier waypoint is a mistake this index exists to prevent.

Closed routes, with the mechanism that closed them

This section is a graveyard with load-bearing headstones. Each entry below is a route that was tried against the \sqrt{}-escape wall (Part III) and failed, but the way it failed is itself a theorem, a computation, or a structural identity that survives the failure. A closed route is not a blank; it is a constraint on every future attempt. We record, for each closure: the route as conceived, the exact mechanism that closed it, the precise scope of the closure (what it rules out and what it leaves untouched), and whatever machinery salvages out of the wreckage. We also flag, for every closure, whether the exclusion is a statement about the (the real number, the achievement set, the actual orbit) or about a of it (a coordinate, a finite-window signature, a proof-route’s hypothesis set). Confusing the two is the single most common way a closed route gets silently re-opened by a later attempt using different words for the same representation.

Throughout, rem(s)\mathrm{rem}(s) is the seam-row remainder, λn:=Δn/2n\lambda_n := \Delta_n/2^n the normalized seam deviation (Part I, SE-3), and 𝒜\mathcal A the Mersenne achievement set. Reset \sqrt{}-escape from row 10 is the statement |rem(r+1)−2r+1|>2(r+5)/2|\mathrm{rem}(r+1)-2^{r+1}| > 2^{(r+5)/2} for every reset row r≥10r\ge 10 (RC-4, Part III); this is the wall every closure below is measured against.

Four closed attack families on the wall itself

Observation 250 (Prime-doubling — closed by explicit counterexample). Route as conceived. The universal recursion K(M+1)=2K(M)−(τ(M+1)−1)K(M+1) = 2K(M) - (\tau(M+1)-1) (Part I, SE-1) doubles at every step and subtracts the divisor-excess τ(M+1)−1\tau(M+1)-1. At a prime M+1=pM+1=p, τ(p)=2\tau(p)=2 so the subtracted term is 11; the naive hope is that primality of an index forces the step to be "almost pure doubling," and that prime density (Chebyshev/PNT-scale) then bounds how long a run of near-pure-doubling steps can last, which would bound the danger run-length LrL_r in SE-3’s equivalence (III).

Exact mechanism that closed it. The hope requires primality to control the recursion , but composite indices subtract more than primes add back, so a long run can mix primes and composites freely without breaking. Certified witness: the run at n=607n=607 spans M∈(607,617]M\in(607,617] with the drift quantity JJ staying in [1,5][1,5] for eleven consecutive steps, and three of the indices inside that window — 607,613,617607,613,617 — are themselves prime. More broadly, of the 40 longest runs found for n≤1500n\le 1500, 26 contain a prime index somewhere inside them. Primality of an index is simply uncorrelated with the recursion staying quiet.

Scope. Closes: any argument that tries to derive a run-length bound on SE-3’s LrL_r, or a bound on the drift JJ in the universal recursion, from prime-counting alone (density, Chebyshev bounds, PNT-scale gap statistics). Does not touch: arguments using the actual value of τ(M+1)−1\tau(M+1)-1 (not just whether M+1M+1 is prime), or any argument working at the divisor-sum level rather than the prime/composite dichotomy. coord:prime-density

Object or representation. About the : the counterexample is a concrete witness inside the actual K(M)K(M) recursion, not an artifact of how the recursion is coordinatized.

Salvage. None as a proof tool — but the witness itself (run length 11 at n=607n=607, 26/40 longest runs prime-touched) is now a banked disconfirming data point: any future prime-density-flavoured attack on run-length should be checked against this witness first. [Cert]

Observation 251 (Parity/perfect-squares — closed as a tautology of the recursion shape). Route as conceived. K(M)K(M) is even exactly when MM is a perfect square (a true, provable fact). The hope was to use this parity law to forbid certain residues or run patterns in the digit stream of KK, since parity constraints are a classical first attack on digit-run questions.

Exact mechanism that closed it. The recursion J(M+1)=2J(M)−δ(M+1)J(M+1) = 2J(M) - \delta(M+1) makes J(M+1)≡δ(M+1)(mod⁡2)J(M+1)\equiv\delta(M+1)\pmod 2 an that this recursion shape produces — it holds regardless of what δ\delta counts, Mersenne-specific or not. The "K(M)K(M) even iff MM a perfect square" fact is real, but it is a restatement of the recursion’s algebraic shape, not new information: it forbids no residue and no run length. It is vacuous as an obstruction because it would hold for recursion of the form J(M+1)=2J(M)−δ(M+1)J(M+1)=2J(M)-\delta(M+1), Mersenne or not.

Scope. Closes: the parity/perfect-square route completely and permanently, for this recursion shape — not a partial closure. Also closes it in advance for any structurally identical recursion (e.g. a hypothetical #249 digit-carry recursion of the same doubling-minus-forcing shape), since the vacuity is a fact about the shape, not about τ\tau or Mersenne weights. coord:parity-tautology

Object or representation. About a : the identity is a fact about the recursion’s algebraic form (base-2 doubling-with-forcing), not about the value K(M)K(M) or the target constant C=E−3/2C=E-3/2 itself. It is empty precisely because it never touches the object.

Salvage. The identity remains true and is a useful sanity check (any proposed digit-run claim about KK must be consistent with it), but it supplies zero constraining power on its own. [Math]

Observation 252 (Irrationality-measure — structurally excluded by an exponent budget). Route as conceived. The wall reduces (SE-2) to: the greedy skip-set sum ∑d∈Skipnxd\sum_{d\in\mathrm{Skip}_n}x_d never approximates C:=E−32=0.1066951524152917…C:=E-\tfrac32=0.1066951524152917\ldots (the shifted Erdős–Borwein constant) to within ∼2−1.5n\sim 2^{-1.5n}. Since CC has a known irrationality-measure upper bound, the natural hope is that a Diophantine-approximation exponent for CC directly supplies the needed non-approximability at scale nn.

Exact mechanism that closed it. The skip-set Skipn\mathrm{Skip}_n has size |Skipn|≈n2/4|\mathrm{Skip}_n|\approx n^2/4 — quadratic in nn, not linear. An irrationality-measure exponent μ\mu for CC bounds how well a rational with denominator qq can approximate CC; specializing to a rational built from ≈n2/4\approx n^2/4 terms only yields a lower bound on the approximation error of order 2−μn2/42^{-\mu n^2/4}, against a required bound of order 2−3n/22^{-3n/2}. The shortfall is a factor of ≈0.42n\approx 0.42n — not a constant-factor gap that a sharper μ\mu could close, but a gap that grows without bound as n→∞n\to\infty for any fixed μ\mu.

Zudilin’s bound μ(E)≤2.42343562…\mu(E)\le 2.42343562\ldots (Math. Notes 72 (2002) 858–862; erratum in Acta Arith. 111 (2004) 153–164 revises this to μ(E)≤2.46497868…\mu(E)\le 2.46497868\ldots) is the best known value, but no future improvement in μ\mu can close this gap, because μ≥2\mu\ge 2 always (a universal lower bound for any irrational number), while the exponent shortfall grows like nn regardless of which fixed μ\mu is plugged in.

Scope. Closes: every attempt to derive the wall from a single-number irrationality-measure statement about CC (or about EE), present or future, as long as the measure is a fixed exponent independent of nn. Does not touch: simultaneous or multi-point Diophantine-approximation results that could in principle scale with the number of terms (no such result is known to exist for this constant, but the exponent-budget argument does not rule out the of one — only the single-exponent route). coord:diophantine-approximation

Object or representation. About the : this is a genuine value-theoretic inequality (an exponent-budget computation), not an artifact of how the skip-set is coordinatized.

Salvage. Flagged in the source corpus as the single strongest reusable negative lemma in the whole programme: any future proposal to attack a Mersenne/Erdős–Borwein-type constant via an irrationality-measure bound should be checked against this exponent-budget argument , before any other work is invested. [Math]

Proposition 253 (2-adic fixed-precision valuation-unit no-go — Lean-verified, problem-agnostic). Route as conceived. A carry orbit’s local 2-adic signature — its valuation and odd unit part at some fixed precision window — looks like a natural finite object to search for a contradiction: if every carry orbit compatible with a given local valuation-unit word were forced outside a safe centred interval, that would be a genuine local obstruction usable at every scale.

Exact mechanism that closed it. For finite word of odd-unit-part valuation symbols at fixed precision u>0u>0, and starting carry state ee, there exists a compatible carry orbit realizing that exact word with every intermediate state staying centred in its dyadic interval, |e′|≤vuRadiusuσ|e'|\le \mathrm{vuRadius}\,u\,\sigma. Bounded local valuation-unit data at fixed precision can never exclude finite centred carry completions — the completion always exists, constructively. ∃states,VUOrbituesymbolsstates∧(∀symbol,|state|≤radius).\exists\,\text{states},\; \mathrm{VUOrbit}\,u\,e\,\text{symbols}\,\text{states} \;\land\; (\forall\,\text{symbol},\, |\text{state}| \le \text{radius}). built from and .

Scope. Closes: any proof strategy that tries to derive a contradiction purely from "the local valuation-unit signature at fixed precision uu is incompatible with XX" — such signatures are realizable by some carry orbit, for every uu and every starting state. Does not touch: arguments using precision (an unbounded window, not a fixed one), or arguments that couple the local signature to extra arithmetic (e.g. a global divisibility or CRT constraint) rather than using the local signature alone. coord:2-adic-valuation-unit

Object or representation. About a : the theorem is entirely about what a bounded local 2-adic window of a carry orbit can and cannot pin down; it says nothing about the target value CC or the achievement set itself. It is a statement that a particular family of finite coordinates (fixed-precision valuation-unit words) is too coarse to see the obstruction, not that no obstruction exists.

Salvage. The theorem is stated and proved for starting carry state and any odd unit-part word — zero arithmetic content beyond 2-adic bookkeeping. It is directly reusable as a hard stop against any future fixed-window 2-adic attack on #249 or #257: a proof needs growing precision or extra coupling, never a fixed local signature alone. [Lean]scale:n/a

Read together, Observations – and Proposition  close every attack family identified against the wall as of this writing that does not go through the digit-level carry machinery itself. What remains open (Part III, and § below) is exactly the digit-carry route — this is not a residual gap after eliminating easier options; it is the one route none of these four mechanisms can even in principle reach, because each closure above excludes a kind of coarse-grained argument (density, tautological parity, single-exponent approximation, fixed-window valuation) while leaving the exact digit recursion itself untouched.

No-go, countermodel, and rigidity modules that bound the wall from outside

The digit-carry route is not merely unclimbed; a family of general-purpose no-go and countermodel results independently constrains can ever close it. These are not about the wall’s numerics — they are about which proof architectures are structurally impossible, for any input.

Proposition 258 (Finite-state no-go: no bounded carry-state summary can recover history). For a "balanced pulse" family at location mm (radius r=(m+1)/2r=(m{+}1)/2, moving mass between positions mm and m+1m{+}1 without changing the series value), if a predecessor state is constant across the whole family, then no function decode:State→ℕ\mathrm{decode}:\mathrm{State}\to\mathbb N can recover the parameter rr from state(r)\mathrm{state}(r) for every rr — fan-out is unbounded (≥⌊m/2⌋+2\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor+2 at m=2km=2k). More strongly, any finite FintypeState\mathrm{Fintype}\ \mathrm{State} needs card(State)≥radius+1\mathrm{card}(\mathrm{State})\ge\mathrm{radius}+1, unbounded in mm. (fan-out lower bound at ).

Scope. Rules out, for #249 or #257, any proof strategy that tries to define a bounded/autonomous "carry state" summarizing pre-mm history and use it to exactly determine the post-mm tail — completely general, no dependence on whether the coefficients are φ\varphi or a Möbius-support indicator. coord:binary-digit, generic Object or representation: about a class (any finite-automaton encoding of history) — it says nothing about CC or 𝒜\mathcal A directly, only that this whole family of encodings is too weak. (exact decomposition at ).

Proposition 260 (No finite support ever hits 1/21/2; finite certificates only ever certify death). No finite positive-index Boolean support has value exactly 1/21/2: the reduced denominator of any finite Mersenne subset-sum is provably odd (each 2n−12^n-1 is odd), while 1/21/2 needs an even denominator. . Separately, 𝖢𝖾𝗋𝗍𝗂𝖿𝗂𝖾𝖽𝖦𝗋𝖾𝖾𝖽𝗒𝖬𝖾𝗋𝗌𝖾𝗇𝗇𝖾𝖣𝖾𝖺𝗍𝗁\mathsf{CertifiedGreedyMersenneDeath} is a decidable, finite-depth certificate proving a real xx is in 𝒜\mathcal A (e.g. 3/43/4 is machine-certified dead at level 1, lookahead 0: ), and this one-sidedness is structural: absence of a found death certificate, or survival through any finite depth, proves about membership. .

Scope. The odd-denominator fact rules out every finite support as a 1/21/2-witness, unconditionally (this is exactly B4/C3 of Part I/III’s cut-locator machinery, and it is why any 1/21/2-achieving support, if one exists, must be genuinely infinite). The one-sidedness caveat rules out treating a finite certified-kill search’s silence as evidence of membership or rationality, for member of the whole certified-kill family (this closure family, #249’s TotientTailPeriodKiller, LcmConeFlatness, etc.) — a structural, not problem-specific, warning that recurs across the entire certificate-based proof programme. coord:parity-denominator / finite-search Object or representation: the odd-denominator fact is about the (value inequality via denominator parity); the one-sidedness caveat is about the (what a finite search, as a proof method, can and cannot show). The mathematics this problem still needs

Everything in Parts I–IV of this document is either an unconditional theorem at a fixed or bounded scale, an exact reformulation, or a producer socket whose supply is missing. None of it decides Erdős #257, and the wall analysis explains why in a way that is more useful than “the problem is hard”: the recorded failures are not a hundred separate defeats but repeated measurements of one obstruction, and the obstruction has a shape. This section takes the next step, which the rest of the corpus did not take. For each surviving route it states the exact statement that is missing, says what of mathematical object would furnish it, names the technique family that is closest and the precise reason that technique does not reach, and where possible attempts an actual construction, estimate or reduction. Attempts are banded honestly: [Math] where the argument is complete ordinary mathematics, [Cert] where the support is exact computation, [Open] where the item is a proposal and nothing more.

The organising fact, established in the wall analysis and not repeated here, is that both halves of #257 — the universal statement and the half-value instance — converge on one missing object. It has a name in this section:

For M≥1M\ge 1 and L≥1L\ge 1 put ΘL(M):=∑i=1L(τ(M+i)−1)2−i∈ℚ≥0,\Theta_L(M)\ :=\ \sum_{i=1}^{L}\bigl(\tau(M+i)-1\bigr)\,2^{-i}\ \in\ \mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}, where τ\tau is the number-of-divisors function, so that τ(n)−1=#{d≥2:d∣n}\tau(n)-1=\#\{d\ge 2: d\mid n\} counts the divisors of nn other than 11.

ΘL\Theta_L is the analytic content of the universal recursion K(2)=1K(2)=1, K(M+1)=2K(M)−(τ(M+1)−1)K(M+1)=2K(M)-(\tau(M+1)-1) that carries the seam deviation (Part II, master identity Δn=K(2n)+∑d∈Skipn⌊4n/(2d−1)⌋\Delta_n = K(2n)+\sum_{d\in\mathrm{Skip}_n}\lfloor 4^n/(2^d-1)\rfloor). It is also, in a sense made precise in §, the universal-direction obstruction written in the divisor incidence coordinate. Every route below either needs a lower bound on dist(ΘL(M),ℤ)\mathrm{dist}(\Theta_L(M),\mathbb{Z}) at a growing precision, or needs to explain why it does not.

What kind of object would furnish it, and the exact arithmetic of ΘL\Theta_L

The first thing to say is what the quantity actually is, because the corpus states it in seam coordinates and that hides its arithmetic nature. The following identity is elementary and exact, and it is the reason this route is an analytic-number-theory problem rather than a combinatorial one.

Lemma 269 (Divisor-residue form of the short-window phase). For all M,L≥1M,L\ge 1, ΘL(M)=∑d≥2∑1≤i≤Li≡−M(modd)2−i=∑d≥22−id(M)⋅1−2−dmd1−2−d,\Theta_L(M)\ =\ \sum_{d\ge 2}\ \sum_{\substack{1\le i\le L\\ i\,\equiv\,-M\ (\mathrm{mod}\ d)}} 2^{-i} \ =\ \sum_{d\ge 2}\ 2^{-i_d(M)}\cdot\frac{1-2^{-d\,m_d}}{1-2^{-d}}, where id(M)∈[1,d]i_d(M)\in[1,d] is the least i≥1i\ge1 with d∣M+id\mid M+i (so id(M)i_d(M) depends only on Mmod⁡dM \operatorname{mod} d), md:=#{i≤L:d∣M+i}m_d := \#\{i\le L: d\mid M+i\}, and terms with id(M)>Li_d(M)>L are empty. Lemma  says the object is the evaluation of a function on the profinite integers along the +1+1-orbit. The corpus’s own Reduction (A), F(n)=∑d∈Dn2d−id(n)/(2d−1)F(n)=\sum_{d\in D_n} 2^{\,d-i_d(n)}/(2^d-1), is ∑d2−id/(1−2−d)\sum_d 2^{-i_d}/(1-2^{-d}) restricted to the greedy take-set DnD_n instead of to all d≥2d\ge2. So the object required is: Unique ergodicity gives equidistribution with no rate. What is needed is a rate, pointwise along a sparse subsequence (the reset rows), at scale 2−r/22^{-r/2} where rr is the index. Equivalently, in the form a specialist will recognise: a lower bound for dist(ΘL(M),ℤ)\mathrm{dist}(\Theta_L(M),\mathbb{Z}) with L≍log⁡2ML\asymp \log_2 M, valid for all large MM in a specified set, at precision 2−L/22^{-L/2}.

Three technique families are the plausible shapes, and it is worth being explicit about which.

τ\tau has an exact Voronoi expansion, and the natural attack is to bound ∑M∈[X,2X]e(aΘL(M))\sum_{M\in[X,2X]} e\bigl(a\,\Theta_L(M)\bigr) for 1≤|a|≤2L1\le|a|\le 2^{L} by opening each τ(M+i)\tau(M+i) and estimating the resulting Kloosterman-type sums. (b) Fourier analysis on ℤ̂\widehat{\mathbb{Z}} / Ramanujan expansions. By Lemma  the phase is a function of MM modulo the dd’s, so its Fourier expansion is over the characters of ℤ/d\mathbb{Z}/d, i.e. over Ramanujan sums cd(⋅)c_d(\cdot); the required estimate becomes decay of the Ramanujan coefficients of ΨL\Psi_L plus a bound on their tails. Prove that the vector (τ(M+1),…,τ(M+L))(\tau(M+1),\dots,\tau(M+L)), L≍log⁡ML\asymp\log M, obeys a limit theorem strong enough to give anti-concentration of the weighted sum at scale 2−L/22^{-L/2}.

The specific obstacle

This is the paragraph worth the most, so it is stated as sharply as the evidence permits.

The interval is logarithmically short, and every unconditional result for divisor sums in short intervals requires the interval to be a power of the modulus. The window [M+1,M+L][M+1,M+L] has length L≍log⁡2ML\asymp\log_2 M. Voronoi-based technology for ∑M<n≤M+Hτ(n)\sum_{M<n\le M+H}\tau(n) — including the Kloosterman-refined results of Deshouillers–Iwaniec type and every subsequent improvement — produces an asymptotic only for H≥MθH\ge M^{\theta} with θ>0\theta>0 fixed, because the dual sum after Voronoi runs to length ∼M/H\sim M/H and the error term is controlled only when that dual length is a power saving against MM.

At H=log⁡MH=\log M the dual sum is of length M/log⁡MM/\log M and there is no saving at all: the method returns the trivial bound. This is not a deficiency of one paper; it is the reason short-interval divisor problems are stated with power-length windows. Technique family (a) is therefore not merely unproved here, it is out of range by an amount in the window length, and no quantitative improvement in Kloosterman bounds changes that, because the obstruction is the length of the dual sum, not the quality of its estimate.

The one technology that does reach sub-power windows delivers the wrong quantifier and the wrong class of function. Matomäki–Radziwiłł theory shows that a multiplicative function bounded by 11 has, in almost all windows [x,x+h][x,x+h] with h→∞h\to\infty arbitrarily slowly, essentially its long average. Two mismatches, both fatal as stated. First, the conclusion is xx, whereas the seam needs reset row r≥31r\ge31; a set of exceptional xx of density zero can still contain every reset row, because the reset rows are themselves a density-zero set defined by the orbit rather than independently of it.

Second, τ\tau is not bounded by 11 and the relevant statistic is not an average of a multiplicative function but the distance to ℤ\mathbb{Z} of a sum of τ\tau-values; the weights 2−i2^{-i} mean that a single value τ(M+1)\tau(M+1) contributes half the phase, so no averaging statement over the window can control it. Anything that averages within the window destroys the quantity, exactly as the wall analysis says of every scale-mismatched tool.

The joint-distribution literature is at CLT scale, not local scale. Erdős–Kac and its descendants, and the Hildebrand–Elliott-type results on the joint normality of ω(n),ω(n+1)\omega(n),\omega(n+1), give distribution functions to accuracy o(1)o(1) and average over n≤Xn\le X. The requirement here is anti-concentration to accuracy 2−L/22^{-L/2} for a fixed LL-tuple of consecutive arguments, i.e. a local limit theorem with an error term exponentially small in LL where L≍log⁡ML\asymp\log M. No result of that strength is known even for L=2L=2.

Why the barrier catalogue predicts exactly this. The wall analysis states that the two available information classes are fixed-precision local arithmetic (killed by , , , all [Lean]) and global Diophantine averages (killed by the exponent-budget computation against μ(E)\mu(E)). The intermediate scale between them is precisely “divisor statistics in logarithmically short windows”, and the three paragraphs above are the reason there is nothing there. The barrier catalogue and the analytic literature agree, independently, on where the gap is.

R3. Prime support: a known theorem and an internal method boundary

The base-22 statement Irrational(∑pprime12p−1)\mathrm{Irrational}\Bigl(\sum_{p\ \mathrm{prime}}\frac1{2^p-1}\Bigr) is known. Expanding geometrically and collecting divisors gives ∑pprime12p−1=∑n≥1ω(n)2n,\sum_{p\ \mathrm{prime}}\frac1{2^p-1} =\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n}, and Tao–Teräväinen prove the latter series irrational in Theorem 1.3 of . This is a cited analytic result, not a theorem formalised in the pinned Lean corpus.

The existing pairwise-coprime Lean theorem does not recover it because that theorem assumes ∑a∈A1/a<∞\sum_{a\in A}1/a<\infty, whereas ∑p1/p\sum_p1/p diverges. Its generic block-certificate engine would also demand, in the prime case, 2r∣ω(N+r)(1≤r≤K),2^r\mid\omega(N+r)\qquad(1\le r\le K), a simultaneous exact divisibility pattern far stronger than the input used by Tao–Teräväinen. Small computational witnesses for K=2,3K=2,3 diagnose that the condition is not vacuous, but they neither prove the known theorem nor define a new open case.

Thus the contribution of this route audit is negative and coordinate-specific: it identifies why the present formal certificate engine fails to reproduce a theorem already available by quantitative correlation estimates. The earlier proposal to prove the prime-support irrationality as new mathematics is withdrawn. Extensions to other bases or prime-power supports are mentioned by the cited authors with proof modifications omitted; this paper promotes only the fully written base-22 theorem.

Why this is a result and not bookkeeping

Under the standing rule that a reduction is not a result, one might discount R4. That would be a mistake, and the reason is the organising thesis of this document. Each biconditional is a theorem, not a reduction: it says a named producer socket is to the goal, hence permanently not easier, hence removable from the list of things worth attempting directly. Five such theorems are a systematic elimination, and a systematic elimination is a statement about the problem. In particular (3) settles the advertised weakening — that no compatibility is required between witness supports at different endpoints — as buying nothing: incompatible witnesses do not create flexibility, because the resulting Π20\Pi^0_2 statement still collapses to the Π10\Pi^0_1 goal.
